entries.1ba34e7b0d4fbb6a: As its corporate philosophy, the company aims to become a company that provides services of encounter, conversation, relaxation and healing to local communities through heart, food and drink, and that is thanked by customers around the world. In the medium to long term, it places importance on sixth-industry initiatives as a “food sixth-industry company” that operates primary (production), secondary (processing) and tertiary (store sales) industries in-house, and its policy is to develop stores that are chosen for improvements in QSCA (quality, service, cleanliness and atmosphere). Its current slogan is “Courage to change, readiness to be changed. Creating the number one local restaurant together,” and the company says it is focusing on strategies to raise store profitability, expanding specialized formats, opening new stores and converting formats, and enabling diverse human resources to thrive.
entries.1c3f6245a3cc22bc: A wide range of customers visit its stores, including people having drinks or banquets with coworkers and families. Franchise owners operate stores under franchise agreements with the company, and in the Contract Business, welfare facilities under the Ministry of Defense and the Ministry of Justice are the entities that commission the operation.
entries.250bd65645188f66: This business consists of operating cafeterias under contract within specific facilities. It operates stores centered on food and beverage service as directly operated stores in welfare facilities under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Defense and the Ministry of Justice, and as of the end of March 2026 it was contracted to operate in 90 facilities nationwide.

entries.596378726d58f4c9: It has a procurement network for fresh seafood that centers on the use of buying rights at Toyosu Market and a consolidated subsidiary at Ota Market, purchases from directly contracted farmers, and a nationwide product supply system centered on distribution centers in Saitama City and three other locations, and it runs food procurement and store supply as one integrated operation built around freshness. In addition, under the “tateuri system,” operations of stores previously run as company-operated stores are transferred to franchise owners, so owners can operate stores expected to generate profit, and the company has built a mechanism to earn royalties and food sales proceeds.

entries.8c535005f730b0ff: Consolidated revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥26,365 million, up 0.6% year on year. Segment information has been omitted, and revenue by category is not disclosed.
entries.9481f712c580543e: This business operates restaurants centered on izakaya (Japanese-style pubs). It operates under formats including 'Hana no Mai' and 'Sakanaya Dojo', with directly operated stores run by the company and franchised stores run by owners under franchise agreements; as of the end of March 2026, the company had 202 directly operated stores and 140 franchised stores, a total of 342 stores. Store product supply is supported by fresh fish procured using bidding rights at Toyosu Market, produce from farmers with whom it has direct contracts, a procurement network through the consolidated subsidiary Ota Ichiba Chimney Co., Ltd., located within the Ota Market of the Tokyo Metropolitan Central Wholesale Market, and a logistics network centered on logistics bases in Saitama City, Saitama Prefecture and 3 other locations. In franchising, the company adopts the 'Tatedate System', under which the operation of stores previously run directly by the company is transferred to owners. The consolidated subsidiaries Beni Fuzu Kopore-shon Co., Ltd. (including 'Shimbashi Yakiton', 19 stores) and Meccha Sakana ga Suki Co., Ltd. (including 'Toyomaru', 9 stores) also operate restaurants, and the equity-method affiliate Tsubohachi Co., Ltd. also runs a food and beverage business.
entries.9cf705a2ee403cc0: Food and beverage service at izakaya stores (Hana no Mai, Sakanaya Dojo, Masuya, Uoboshi, Yakiniku Gyusei, etc.).
entries.a761989f5f6d7093: Net income attributable to owners of the parent for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥504 million, down 53.1% year on year. The company's analysis cites as a factor its inability to fully absorb cost increases, including raw material prices and personnel expenses.
entries.a909a8bb75a7e8a8: Operation of izakaya stores and contract operation of in-facility cafeterias.
entries.b10bb7220359e644: The food service industry, centered on izakaya restaurants, faces a difficult environment in which declining domestic population, a low birthrate and aging society, labor shortages, rising costs such as raw material and personnel expenses, and intensifying competition between companies continue, and the company recognizes that customers' inclination to save and to be selective is also strengthening. Within this environment, the company identifies as its challenge becoming a store that customers choose, while attracting customers through seasonal fairs and by capturing banquet demand.

entries.b6d60001e2a1395a: The business model is to operate izakaya restaurants through company-operated and franchised stores, earning revenue from food and beverage service at stores, royalties and food sales from franchised stores, and contract operation of in-facility cafeterias.
